land.text: Bactria and the five xihou, united when 'the Kushana, become dominant' (c. 30 CE) under Kujula Kadphises

successors.note: Cliopatria's Kushan row begins in 43. Continuity is strong (one of the five Yuezhi principalities absorbing the others); a reviewer may prefer a rename inside one dossier, but the Kushan Empire is another group's (sa-02) and has its own row.

capitals.name: Court north of the Gui (Oxus), city not named
capitals.note: Zhang Qian: 'the Great Yuezhi live 2,000 or 3,000 li ... west of [Dayuan], north of the Gui [Oxus] river' (Yuezhi page); 'The Yuezhi court was on the northern bank of the Oxus (Gui) River' (Zhang Qian page). The point is the middle Oxus near Termez, the researcher's placement; no seat is named for the Hexi or Ili periods.

The page puts the Yuezhi 'between Dunhuang and Qilian' and 'powerful near Dunhuang, near the western end of the Hexi Corridor' before 221 BCE; the Kushan page 'in eastern Xinjiang and northwestern Gansu'. Corrected to Hexi plus the Xinjiang part of the drawn shape. No infobox area exists; the Shiji's '100,000 or 200,000 archer warriors' is the only size given.

Modu 'defeated them in 203 BCE' without taking land; the Tarim and eastern Xinjiang went in 178 BCE ('the Xiongnu overran the Yuezhi and Wusun in Gansu and the Tarim Basin') and Hexi in 176 BCE, so the shape should end in 177 with the Xinjiang part gone from 178 (ledger).

correction.text: the Ili valley 'immediately north of the Tian Shan mountains', holding from 165 BCE

keyframe_review.note: The Ili valley (0.16 M km2): right in place, five years early. 'The majority of the Yuezhi begin migrating west to the Ili valley' in 165 BCE ('in about 165 BC ... immediately north of the Tian Shan mountains'); the Greco-Bactrian and Wusun pages say 162 BCE. Between 176 and 166 the Yuezhi were in flight and held no settled land.

correction.text: the shape as drawn to 132 BCE; then without the Ili valley, which the Wusun took, and with Sogdia and the north bank of the Oxus from 130 BCE (ledger)

keyframe_review.note: The shape adds the land west of the Ili towards Sogdia from 144 BCE, but the Yuezhi lost the Ili only in 132 BCE ('In 132 BC the Wusun, in alliance with the Xiongnu, drove them from the Ili valley') and 'migrate west, then south and settle in north-west Bactria' in 132-130 BCE. As drawn it is right for the Ili to 132; after 132 the Ili belongs to the Wusun and the Yuezhi are on the Oxus.

But the shape still reaches 45.5 N, the Ili, which the Wusun held from 132 BCE: removed.

region.text: 'between Dunhuang and Qilian' and eastern Xinjiang

ledger.note: 404 BCE: the Yuezhi hold the Hexi Corridor between Dunhuang and Qilian. 'In the past, they lived in the region between Dunhuang and Qilian' (Shiji, quoted on the page); earliest mentions in the Tale of King Mu (early 4th century BCE) and the Yi Zhou Shu; 'The Yuezhi are powerful near Dunhuang, near the western end of the Hexi Corridor' before 221 BCE. The year is Cliopatria's; no page dates a founding.

region.text: the Hexi Corridor between Dunhuang and Qilian

ledger.note: 203 BCE: Modu's war on the Yuezhi. 'The second war took place in the seventh year of Modu's reign (203 BCE)' (Yuezhi page); Modu 'defeated them in 203 BCE' (Modu Chanyu page); Xiongnu raids had begun in 207 BCE.

region.text: 'the Yuezhi and Wusun in Gansu and the Tarim Basin': the Xinjiang part of the homeland

ledger.note: 178 BCE: the Xiongnu overrun the Tarim and eastern Xinjiang. 'In 178 BCE, the Xiongnu overran the Yuezhi and Wusun in Gansu and the Tarim Basin' (Modu Chanyu page); the Laoshang page dates a Tarim campaign to 164 BCE.
176 BCE: the Xiongnu drive the Yuezhi from Hexi. 'In 176 BC, when the Xiongnu drove them from the Hexi Corridor and killed their king' (Xiongnu page).

176 BCE: the Yuezhi lose the Hexi Corridor and their king. 'the Xiongnu drove them from the Hexi Corridor and killed their king' (Xiongnu page); Laoshang 'had their king's skull into a drinking cup, then drove them from Gansu' in '177 or 176 BCE' (Laoshang page); 'Circa 176 BCE | The Xiongnu inflict a major defeat on the Yuezhi' (Yuezhi page). The Lesser Yuezhi stayed in the Qilian mountains among the Qiang, no longer a state; the Greater Yuezhi fled west.

region.text: the Ili valley, 'immediately north of the Tian Shan mountains'

ledger.note: 165 BCE: the Yuezhi settle the Ili valley. The Greater Yuezhi 'began migrating north-west in about 165 BC' and 'settled first in the Ili valley, immediately north of the Tian Shan mountains', where they 'reportedly displaced elements of the Sakas' (Yuezhi page); the Greco-Bactrian page: 'In 162 BC the Yuezhi were driven west to the Ili River valley'; the Wusun page 'c. 162 BC'.

132 BCE: the Wusun take the Ili. 'In 132 BC the Wusun, in alliance with the Xiongnu,' drove the Yuezhi from the Ili valley (Yuezhi page); 'Liejiaomi attacked the Yuezhi in the Ili Valley, and the Wusun settled the area' c. 133-132 BCE (Wusun page). The Yuezhi 'migrate west, then south and settle in north-west Bactria' (132-130 BCE).

region.text: Sogdia and 'the northern bank of the Oxus, in the region of northern Bactria'

ledger.note: 130 BCE: the Yuezhi settle Sogdia and the north bank of the Oxus. They 'migrated southward to Sogdia and later settled in Bactria', 'on the northern bank of the Oxus, in the region of northern Bactria' (Yuezhi page, timeline 132-130 BCE). The Greco-Bactrian page gives no date for the loss of Sogdia; eastern Scythians had been invading 'various parts of Parthia and Bactria' since around 140 BCE and Ai-Khanoum burned around 145 BCE.

126 BCE: Bactria south of the Oxus comes 'under their sway'. Zhang Qian's account, given in 126 BCE: 'the Yuezhi were settled north of the Oxus but also held under their sway the territory south of Oxus'; 'After the Great Yuezhi moved west and attacked Daxia, the entire country came under their sway' (Greco-Bactrian page). The same page dates the southward expansion 'around 120 BC' and the kingdom's end c. 120 BCE; the Kushan page: 'the Kushans (Guishuang) divided up Bactria in 128 BC'. Cliopatria's 126 is within the range.

42: Kujula Kadphises' Kushans absorb the five xihou. 'Circa 30 CE | One of five tribes comprising the Great Yuezhi tribes, the Kushana, become dominant' and the Guishuang xihou 'attacked and exterminated the four other xihou' (Yuezhi page); Kujula 'united the Yuezhi confederation in Bactria during the 1st century CE' and invaded Indo-Parthia 'some time after 45 CE' (Kujula page); the Kushan infobox dates the confederation to 30 CE. Cliopatria hands over in 42/43; the Han kept calling the Kushans 'Da Yuezhi'.

wars.name: Xiongnu–Yuezhi wars

zones.text: the Tarim Basin and eastern Xinjiang

wars.outcome: Xiongnu victory: three wars (under Touman; 203 BCE; 'before or in 176 BCE'); the Yuezhi king killed and the Yuezhi driven from Hexi in 176 BCE; Modu's letter of 174 BCE claims to have wiped them out.

wars.name: Yuezhi–Wusun war
wars.outcome: Yuezhi victory without territorial change: 'c. 173 BC: The Yuezhi attacked the Wusun and killed their king, Nandoumi'; the Wusun took refuge with the Xiongnu.

wars.name: Wusun conquest of the Ili
wars.outcome: Wusun victory: the Yuezhi driven from the Ili to Sogdia and Bactria; the Wusun settle the Ili.

wars.name: Yuezhi conquest of Bactria
wars.outcome: Yuezhi victory: Bactria 'came under their sway' by 126 BCE; the Greco-Bactrian kingdom disestablished c. 120 BCE, its successors the Indo-Greek, Parthian and Kushan states.
wars.note: Strabo's tribes 'who deprived the Greeks of Bactriana': Asii, Pasiani, Tochari, Sacarauli; Heliocles I 'was the last Greek king to rule in Bactria' (dates conflict: 140-130 or 117-100 BCE).

certainty.note: Nomadic ranges throughout: the Hexi homeland, the Ili valley and the Oxus lands are approximate; the Oxus itself is the one natural line (Zhang Qian's north bank/south bank).

notes:
Written by the ia-01-a research agent on 2026-10-18 from nine pages (six opened for the Yuezhi, three shared with the Xiongnu dossier).

Cliopatria's homeland shapes (404-171 BCE) lie between 72 and 93.5 E, west of Dunhuang and into Kazakhstan and Kyrgyzstan, while every page puts the Yuezhi 'between Dunhuang and Qilian' (Hexi) and in eastern Xinjiang: corrected to Hexi plus the Xinjiang part of the drawn shape. The Ili shape is five years early (165 BCE), the Ili lingers in the 144, 126 and 63 BCE shapes after the Wusun took it in 132 BCE, and the handover to the Kushan row (43) falls within the pages' range for Kujula's unification (c. 30-45 CE).

Start 404 BCE is Cliopatria's: the pages give only textual mentions from the 4th century BCE (confidence 1). The Lesser Yuezhi, who stayed in the Qilian mountains among the Qiang after 176 BCE, are not a state and are not drawn.

Counterparts without dossiers: the Sakas of the Ili ('displaced elements of the Sakas', 165 BCE; counterpart 'sakas', ia-01-x scope). The Bactrian gains are charged to greco-bactrian-kingdom (me-05), whose page gives no date for the loss of Sogdia; its dossier should carry the losses c. 130-120 BCE.

Infobox: no area figure on any page; the Shiji's '100,000 or 200,000 archer warriors' and the Hanshu's '100,000 households, 400,000 people' are the only sizes.
